coupons.note: Everything sells at MRP, so a coupon is the only discount there is. Four digits, because they get read out over a counter and typed on a phone. 1626 is the real one; the rest are spares to hand out. Codes are matched case-insensitively and with spaces stripped, since nobody types them carefully. Add or remove codes here -- no code change. Set `percent` to 0 to switch coupons off entirely.

delivery.note: Delivery is free on every order, at every distance, with no threshold, and there is NO minimum order -- `minOrder: 0`. `freeAlways` is what the UI reads to say the first part out loud rather than silently charging nothing. The minimum-order arithmetic is still in domain.js and still tested, because switching one back on should be this number and nothing else.

demoNote: OFF. While true, app/seed.js drops a few INVENTED orders onto the next window, but only on a device that has never been used -- so the Store board is not empty the first time someone is shown this. Turned off so the app starts genuinely blank. Flip it back to true and clear the browser data (Settings has a button) to get the demo world again.

festival.note: The festive shelf. It shows itself between `from` and `to` (IST dates, inclusive) and then takes itself down -- nobody has to remember to remove it, which is the only reason a seasonal banner is safe to ship at all. THE SHOPKEEPER SETS THE DATES: he knows when Diwali is and the app does not compute it, because the festival calendar is lunar and a wrong guess would put a greeting on the wrong fortnight. `id` picks the wording out of i18n.js -- with an id nothing is written for, no banner is drawn at all. Products are shown in the order listed, so put the thing you most want sold first.

llSource: A point on Devidas Road, confirmed by reverse geocoding (Nominatim returns `Devidas Road ... 400103`, matching the written address on street and postcode). Accurate to 200-300 m. Only used to show the shop's own location now that the delivery route has been parked.
note: EVERYTHING THE SHOPKEEPER OWNS, in one file. Name, address, phone, UPI, and what delivery costs. Nothing here needs a code change. It is JSON rather than config.js so the Perl checks can read it too.

offers.note: Buy 2 get 1 free. Every THIRD unit of the SAME product is free: 2 cost 2, 3 cost 2, 6 cost 4, 7 cost 5. Integer division, so it can never hand out part of a packet. These are the small snack packs people already buy several of -- the offer has to be on something a basket naturally holds three of, or it is decoration. Add or remove ids here and nothing else changes; an empty list switches the offer off completely. ORDER OF OPERATIONS: the free unit is priced out BEFORE a coupon is applied, so the coupon discounts what is actually owed and the two never multiply.

staff.note: The code that opens the Store view. The code ITSELF is not here and cannot be recovered from this file -- `proof` is PBKDF2-SHA256 of it (600000 iterations), which only runs one way. To change the code: perl tools/setpin.pl <6 digits>, then commit and push. To remove the gate and let anyone open the Store view: perl tools/setpin.pl --off. Forgotten codes cannot be looked up; set a new one.

upi.note: A DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVABLE id, so the pay button and QR can be shown in a demo with no chance of money moving. `example` is not a real UPI handle -- no payment provider owns it -- so a UPI app opens, fails to resolve the id and stops. Money cannot reach a stranger, which was the only thing that made a dummy id risky. While `demo` is true the app prints a visible DEMO strip across the pay block in all three languages, so nobody tries to pay it in earnest. TO GO LIVE: put the shop's real UPI id here (e.g. 8169022727@ybl or milansupershoppe@okaxis), set `demo` to false, and the strip disappears by itself.
upi.phoneNote: Shown on the pay screen beside the UPI id, for a customer typing it into their own UPI app rather than scanning. The shop's OWN number on purpose: an invented one would resolve in a UPI app and could send a customer's money to whoever really owns it, which is the one thing the unresolvable @example id is there to prevent. Change it only to another number this shop controls.
